_note: REAL row from production.supply_analytics.sxp_activity_criteria, exported 2026-06-08 – 2026-10-14. Scalar fields are verbatim. `supplier_name` came with the export this time, as it did for bft-ts, so no dwh.dim_supplier lookup was needed. The export also carried a `supplier_email` (a personal gmail address); it is DROPPED here — this repo publishes to a public GitHub Pages site and the fixture JSON is readable in page source.
_note_booking_detail: The export's raw `dbr_tags` (7 rows), `pickup_problem_rate.applicable_records` (1 row) and `trust_and_safety_tags` (empty) arrays are dropped here, matching every other fixture — the page has nowhere to show per-booking rows. They are summarised into details.quality-rate.disruptions and details.pickup-rate.disruptions below.
_note_next_award_date: NOT from the export. Set to the close of the intended assessment period (2027-01-01), matching every other fixture so the banner reads the same across the switcher. Award cadence is still an open question in the criteria deck.
_note_window: window_start/window_end are the INTENDED assessment period (Jul 1, 2026 – Jan 1, 2027), not this row's own export window (2026-06-08 – 2026-10-14). The metrics below were measured over the export window, so the period label and the numbers come from different ranges — the same deliberate mismatch activity-21293 documents, kept consistent here so every fixture in the switcher shows one period.

details._note: Built from the export's own `dbr_tags` array, counting DISTINCT booking_id per tag and filtered to the tag sets the criteria deck defines: the 9 quality tags + Supplier Cancellation (non-FM) for `quality-rate`, the 2 pickup tags for `pickup-rate`. One tag is excluded by that filter — `Payment issues or double charge` (category Payment Problems), which is not one of the nine. Note `Activity Not As Advertised` appears three times in the raw array but on only TWO distinct bookings: booking 413783538 carries it from both `review` and `care_chat` sources. Counting rows rather than bookings would have overstated it.
details._caveat_counts_reconcile_here: UNUSUALLY, the counts below reconcile exactly. The three quality tags cover distinct bookings {413783538, 415723727, 436223746} = 3, matching quality_defect_bookings = 3; the single pickup tag covers booking 433100106 = 1, matching pickup_defect_bookings = 1. This is the rare case — measured across the warehouse, only about 1.2% of activities with a non-zero quality rate have booking-level tags that fully account for the rate (see CLAUDE.md, 'sxp_booking_defect does not reconcile'). It reconciles here because this fixture's detail comes from the export's own embedded `dbr_tags` array rather than from a separate query against sxp_booking_defect, and because the window ends before that table's coverage gap bites. Do not generalise from it.
details._caveat_trend_invented: Both `trend` series are INVENTED. No monthly series exists anywhere — a monthly rate needs a monthly denominator and sxp_activity_criteria holds only the window aggregate, while a monthly rating series has no source at all. Only each series' mean is anchored to a real value; the month-to-month shape is illustrative and uses the same fixed zero-sum pattern as the other fixtures.

details._note_pickup_hidden: The pickup-rate breakdown below is built but NOT rendered: has_pickup is false, so criteria-model.js hides the Pickup Problem Rate row entirely. Note this activity is another instance of the has_pickup=false anomaly documented in CLAUDE.md — it has no pickup, yet the export still carries a pickup tag and a pickup rate for it. It is NOT one of the 112 whose badge turns on that bug, since it fails the quality rate independently.

activity_title: Kyoto: 100% Private Tea Ceremony, Calligraphy, and Kimono
_note_city_bar: This row is BLOCKED BY THE CITY BAR, the third fixture to exercise badge.blockedByCityBar after italy-rating and italy-defect, and the first outside Italy. Kyoto is destination_step 8, so its quality bar is 0.50% rather than the 2.00% global minimum. The activity's 0.845% clears the global bar (crit_defect_rate_min = true) but not Kyoto's (crit_defect_rate = false), which is exactly the condition the model tests: !earnedBadge(a) && earnedBadge(a, true).
_note_details_rating: INVENTED, not from the export. Six points generated around the row's real rating_in_window (4.9545) with the same fixed zero-sum shape the other fixtures use, scaled so the series stays under 5.0 and clears the 4.80 bar in every month, matching crit_rating = true. Rounded to 2dp as elsewhere, which drifts the mean slightly: 4.9517 against the real 4.9545. Only the mean is anchored to anything real.
_note_details_quality_rate: INVENTED, not from the export. Six points generated around the row's real quality_defect_rate (0.8451%) with the same fixed zero-sum shape, scaled so every month sits ABOVE the 0.50% city bar — matching crit_defect_rate = false, so the chart shades all six months rather than just some. Only the mean is anchored to anything real.
